title: VPC Collector: air-gapped export format + offline reconciliation for quota/cap correctness
creator: Priya Kapoor
description: Context: Private/VPC customers run on-prem collectors in air-gapped environments. Current onprem usage exporters create monolithic bundles that are difficult to reconcile against the hosted ledger when syncs are delayed, and they lack explicit rate-cap context, causing quota accounting drift and duplicate charge risk. Goal: design and implement a compact, backwards-compatible air-gapped export format and offline reconciliation pipeline that preserves per-tenant rate-cap / quota metadata, supports idempotent ingestion, and produces deterministic deltas for ledger reconciliation. The solution must work within constrained upload windows (single-file transport or removable media), be resilient to partial-bundles and replays, and provide clear audit trails for billing and dispute resolution.
acceptance_criteria: Export bundle schema v2 defined and documented (fields: tenant_id, export_window_start, export_window_end, sequence_range, per-tenant-ratecap_snapshot, compact delta list, checksum, signer metadata)
Collector produces signed bundle files and an accompanying lightweight manifest with a Bloom filter summary to detect overlapping sequences without full transfer
Ingestion service accepts bundles idempotently and records bundle provenance (file id, signer, checksum, arrival_time)

Reconciliation job computes deterministic deltas against hosted ledger, flags conflicts (overlap, missing sequences, rate-cap changes) and generates human-readable dispute artifacts within 1 hour of bundle ingestion
Automated alerts for high-value conflicts (> $1000/day discrepancy) and delayed replays (> 72 hours) wired to SRE/Finance Slack channel
E2E test harness simulates out-of-order bundle arrival, duplicate replays, and partial-bundle recovery with >= 95% reconciliation accuracy on synthetic traces
Docs/Runbook and customer-facing KB article describing how to export, sign, and ship bundles are published
updates: 2025-02-18 - Ticket created after customer incident where an onprem customer shipped two overlapping bundles; billing team detected duplicates requiring manual refunds. Recorded incident ticket #INC-590.

2025-02-20 - Design sync with Security, Billing, and Solutions teams. Decided to include per-tenant 'ratecap_snapshot' to capture active quota windows and burst allowances at export time to disambiguate accepted vs rejected requests in offline period.
2025-02-24 - Spike: implemented prototype exporter that emits sequence ranges + Bloom summary. Tested on small cluster; Bloom false positive rate tuned to 0.01 with 128-byte summary per tenant.
2025-02-28 - Review feedback from Billing: require signer+KMS fingerprint and canonicalization to support long-term audit. Security requested signed manifests only (no private keys in collector).
2025-03-01 - Backend ingestion stub merged (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/collector/bundle-ingest PR#1221). Added initial idempotency keyed by (tenant_id, bundle_id, checksum).

2025-03-02 - Reconciliation algorithm prototype demonstrates deterministic merge for 98% of replay sequences on synthetic dataset; remaining cases are concurrent quota changes during offline window. Plan: add conflict policy 'hosted-wins' with explicit dispute artifact for manual review.
notes: Key trade-offs considered: include full per-request logs (largest, simpler) vs compact delta encoding with Bloom filters (smaller, adds FP complexity). We chose compact deltas + signed manifests to keep bundle sizes manageable for physical transport while ensuring strong provenance. Also debating whether to ship per-tenant watermark ledger inside bundle vs separate ledger snapshots; current plan is separate snapshot + sequence ranges for simpler ledger merges. Follow-ups: implement analytics job to quantify how often 'concurrent quota-change' conflicts occur so we can iterate on conflict policy.
